neighbours.label: start of the implied speech a look, gesture or expression 'says' ('a look that said, I'm ...')
fire: Across the table, my mother shot me a glare that said, 'Don't you dare.'
The cat stared at the empty bowl with an expression that seemed to say, 'Feed me now.'
He raised one eyebrow, a gesture that clearly meant, 'You can't be serious.'
Without a word, the coach gave us a nod that said, 'Good job, boys.'
Her folded arms told me plainly, 'I'm not leaving until you apologize.'
The old man smiled as if to say he had known all along.
When I walked in late, the teacher's eyes said, 'We'll talk about this later.'
The dog tilted its head as though asking, 'Are we going for a walk?'
quiet: Across the table, my mother leaned over and whispered, 'Don't you dare.'
The cat stared at the empty bowl while I said, 'I'll feed you soon.'
He raised one hand and asked the waiter, 'Can we get the check?'
Without a pause, the coach shouted at us, 'Run it again, boys.'
Her letter told me plainly that she was leaving town on Friday.
The old man smiled and told us he had lived there all his life.
When I walked in late, the teacher announced, 'Page forty, everyone.'
The dog tilted its head and then trotted toward the door.
